title: Appointment reminder templates for text and email
summary: Copy-ready appointment reminder texts and emails for doctors, dentists, and clinics, with SMS character counts, opt-out wording, and what to leave out.
body_markdown:
A good appointment reminder template answers four questions: who it's from, when and where the appointment is, how to confirm or reschedule, and how to stop getting texts. It leaves out why the patient is coming in. That last part matters more in healthcare than anywhere else, because a reminder lands on a lock screen, on a phone the whole family uses, and sometimes on a number that's been reassigned.


Below are 35 copy-ready appointment reminder templates:text templates for every point in the booking cycle,email templates with subject lines and preview text, and short sets for doctors, dentists, therapists, and other practices. Every text fits in a single 160-character SMS segment and includes opt-out wording.


## What to include and what to leave out


Include Leave out


Your practice or provider name The reason for the visit


Date and time Diagnoses, conditions, or symptoms


A general location, address, or parking note Procedure or test names


A confirm or reschedule link, or a phone number Medication names


How to opt out ("Reply STOP to opt out") A specialty that reveals a condition ("oncology," "behavioral health")


Balances, copays, or fees


HIPAA's minimum necessary standard doesn't apply to disclosures made to the patient ([45 CFR 164.502(b)(2)](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-45/subtitle-A/subchapter-C/part-164/subpart-E/section-164.502) ), so this isn't a legal line. It's the safe default, and it's Courier's recommendation: keep protected health information (PHI) out of the message and put the details behind a login. For the full reasoning, see[is texting patients a HIPAA violation?](https://www.courier.com/blog/is-texting-patients-a-hipaa-violation)


Patients can also ask to be contacted a specific way, and providers must accommodate reasonable requests to receive communications by alternative means ([45 CFR 164.522(b)](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-45/subtitle-A/subchapter-C/part-164/subpart-E/section-164.522) ). If someone asks for email only, honor it.


**How to use these templates:**


- Variables are written as` {{clinic_name}}` ,` {{date}}` ,` {{time}}` ,` {{clinic_phone}}` ,` {{confirm_url}}` , and so on. Swap in whatever syntax your tool uses.
- Character counts are for the template as written. Real values change the count. With a 19-character clinic name, a 12-character phone number, and 30-character links, every text below still fits in 160. Check yours in the[SMS segment counter](https://www.courier.com/tools/sms-segment-counter) .
- Use full links on your own domain, not public link shorteners, which carriers often filter.
- Keep straight quotes and plain punctuation. One curly apostrophe or emoji switches the whole text to UCS-2 encoding, which drops the limit from 160 characters to 70.


## Appointment reminder text templates


Pick two or three per appointment, not all of them. Seetiming and channel mix for sequences.


### Booking confirmation


Text


```text
{{clinic_name}}: you're booked for {{date}} at {{time}}. To change it, visit {{confirm_url}} or call {{clinic_phone}}. Reply STOP to opt out.
```


Characters: 141 as written.


### 7 days before


Text


```text
{{clinic_name}}: reminder, your appointment is in one week, {{date}} at {{time}}. Need a new time? Call {{clinic_phone}}. Reply STOP to opt out.
```


Characters: 144 as written.


### 72 hours before


Text


```text
{{clinic_name}}: your appointment is {{date}} at {{time}}. Confirm: {{confirm_url}} To reschedule, call {{clinic_phone}}. Reply STOP to opt out.
```


Characters: 144 as written.


### 24 hours before, reply to confirm


Text


```text
{{clinic_name}}: see you tomorrow at {{time}}. Reply C to confirm or R to reschedule. Questions? {{clinic_phone}}. Reply STOP to opt out.
```


Characters: 137 as written.


Reply keywords need inbound SMS handling on your side: a "C" marks the appointment confirmed, an "R" triggers a call or a reschedule link. Never ask patients to reply CANCEL to cancel a visit. CANCEL is one of the opt-out words carriers expect you to honor, so that patient has also unsubscribed from your texts.


### 24 hours before, link to confirm


Text


```text
{{clinic_name}}: see you tomorrow at {{time}}. Confirm or reschedule: {{confirm_url}} Questions? {{clinic_phone}}. Reply STOP to opt out.
```


Characters: 137 as written.


### 2 hours before


Text


```text
{{clinic_name}}: see you today at {{time}} at {{address}}. Running late? Call {{clinic_phone}}. Reply STOP to opt out.
```


Characters: 118 as written.


### Day-of arrival and parking


Text


```text
{{clinic_name}}: welcome! Park in the Oak St garage and check in at the front desk on floor 2. Questions? {{clinic_phone}}. Reply STOP to opt out.
```


Characters: 146 as written. Replace the parking line with your own.


### Telehealth link, 30 minutes before


Text


```text
{{clinic_name}}: your video visit starts at {{time}}. Join here: {{visit_url}} Trouble connecting? Call {{clinic_phone}}. Reply STOP to opt out.
```


Characters: 144 as written.


### Reschedule confirmation


Text


```text
{{clinic_name}}: your appointment is now {{date}} at {{time}}. Need another change? Call {{clinic_phone}}. Reply STOP to opt out.
```


Characters: 129 as written.


### Cancellation confirmation


Text


```text
{{clinic_name}}: your {{date}} appointment is canceled. Book a new time at {{booking_url}} or call {{clinic_phone}}. Reply STOP to opt out.
```


Characters: 139 as written.


### No-show follow-up


Text


```text
{{clinic_name}}: we missed you today. Book a new time at {{booking_url}} or call {{clinic_phone}}. Reply STOP to opt out.
```


Characters: 121 as written. Leave missed-appointment fees out of the text. Billing content takes the text out of the healthcare exemption in the Telephone Consumer Protection Act (TCPA).


### Waitlist opening


Text


```text
{{clinic_name}}: an earlier time opened up, {{date}} at {{time}}. Reply Y to take it. Questions? {{clinic_phone}}. Reply STOP to opt out.
```


Characters: 137 as written. Send it to one patient at a time, or tell later replies the slot is gone.


## Appointment reminder email templates


Email has room for what a text doesn't: an address, parking, what to bring, and a calendar button. Keep the subject line and preview text as generic as the body, since both show up in inbox lists and notifications. The[calendar link generator](https://www.courier.com/tools/calendar-link-generator) builds the "add to calendar" links.


Every email below ends with the same footer:


Text


```text
{{clinic_name}} | {{address}} | {{clinic_phone}}
Manage your notification preferences: {{preferences_url}}
```


### Booking confirmation email


Text


```text
Subject: You're booked for {{date}} at {{time}}
Preview: Add it to your calendar, or change it if you need to.


Hi {{first_name}},


You're booked at {{clinic_name}} on {{date}} at {{time}}.


Where: {{address}}
Add to calendar: {{calendar_url}}


Need to change it? Reschedule or cancel at {{reschedule_url}}, or call us at {{clinic_phone}}.


See you then,
{{clinic_name}}
```


### 72-hour reminder email


Text


```text
Subject: Your appointment is on {{date}}
Preview: How to confirm, and what to bring.


Hi {{first_name}},


Your appointment at {{clinic_name}} is on {{date}} at {{time}}.


Before you come in:
- Confirm your appointment: {{confirm_url}}
- Fill out any forms in your patient portal: {{portal_url}}
- Bring your insurance card and a photo ID


Can't make it? Reschedule at {{reschedule_url}} or call {{clinic_phone}}.
```


### 24-hour reminder email


Text


```text
Subject: See you tomorrow at {{time}}
Preview: Address, parking, and check-in details.


Hi {{first_name}},


A reminder that your appointment at {{clinic_name}} is tomorrow, {{date}}, at {{time}}.


Address: {{address}}
Parking: {{parking_info}}


Please arrive 10 minutes early to check in. Running late or need a new time? Call {{clinic_phone}} or reschedule at {{reschedule_url}}.
```


### Telehealth email


Text


```text
Subject: Your video visit is on {{date}} at {{time}}
Preview: Your link, plus how to get set up.


Hi {{first_name}},


Your video visit with {{clinic_name}} is on {{date}} at {{time}}.


Join here: {{visit_url}}


Before your visit:
- Use a phone or computer with a camera and microphone
- Find a quiet, private spot
- Open the link a few minutes early to test your connection


Trouble connecting? Call {{clinic_phone}}.
```


### Reschedule confirmation email


Text


```text
Subject: Your appointment has moved to {{date}}
Preview: Your new time is {{time}}. The old one is canceled.


Hi {{first_name}},


Your appointment at {{clinic_name}} is now on {{date}} at {{time}}. Your previous time is canceled, so there's nothing else you need to do.


Where: {{address}}
Add to calendar: {{calendar_url}}


Need another change? Visit {{reschedule_url}} or call {{clinic_phone}}.
```


### No-show email


Text


```text
Subject: We missed you today
Preview: Book a new time that works for you.


Hi {{first_name}},


We missed you at your appointment today. It happens.


When you're ready, book a new time at {{booking_url}} or call us at {{clinic_phone}}.


{{clinic_name}}
```


### Annual checkup recall email


Text


```text
Subject: It's time for your yearly checkup
Preview: Book a visit at a time that works for you.


Hi {{first_name}},


It's been about a year since your last checkup at {{clinic_name}}. Book your next one at {{booking_url}}, or call us at {{clinic_phone}} and we'll find a time.


See you soon,
{{clinic_name}}
```


## Templates by practice type


These sets cover what changes by specialty. The rule gets stricter as the specialty gets more sensitive: the sender name and` {{clinic_name}}` should never describe the care.


### Doctor and primary care


**What to bring:**


Text


```text
{{clinic_name}}: see you {{date}} at {{time}}. Bring your insurance card and photo ID. Questions? {{clinic_phone}}. Reply STOP to opt out.
```


Characters: 138 as written.


**New patient forms:**


Text


```text
{{clinic_name}}: new patient? Fill out your forms before {{date}}: {{forms_url}} Questions? {{clinic_phone}}. Reply STOP to opt out.
```


Characters: 132 as written.


**Annual checkup recall:**


Text


```text
{{clinic_name}}: it's time for your annual checkup. Book at {{booking_url}} or call {{clinic_phone}}. Reply STOP to opt out.
```


Characters: 124 as written.


### Dental and dentist


**24-hour reminder:**


Text


```text
{{clinic_name}}: your dental visit is tomorrow at {{time}}. Reply C to confirm or R to reschedule. Questions? {{clinic_phone}}. Reply STOP to opt out.
```


Characters: 150 as written.


**Six-month recall:**


Text


```text
{{clinic_name}}: you're due for your six-month checkup. Book at {{booking_url}} or call {{clinic_phone}}. Reply STOP to opt out.
```


Characters: 128 as written.


**Overdue recall:**


Text


```text
{{clinic_name}}: it's been a while since your last checkup. Book at {{booking_url}} or call {{clinic_phone}}. Reply STOP to opt out.
```


Characters: 132 as written.


Name the visit type only for routine care like a checkup. Treatment visits get "your appointment."


### Behavioral health and therapy


**Appointment reminder:**


Text


```text
{{clinic_name}}: reminder of your appointment {{date}} at {{time}}. To change it, call {{clinic_phone}}. Reply STOP to opt out.
```


Characters: 127 as written.


**Video appointment:**


Text


```text
{{clinic_name}}: your appointment starts at {{time}}. Join: {{visit_url}} Questions? {{clinic_phone}}. Reply STOP to opt out.
```


Characters: 125 as written.


Use the practice's neutral business name, not a name that describes the care. Write "appointment," never "therapy" or "counseling."


### Physical therapy


**Next session:**


Text


```text
{{clinic_name}}: your next session is {{date}} at {{time}}. Wear clothes you can move in. Questions? {{clinic_phone}}. Reply STOP to opt out.
```


Characters: 141 as written.


**Next visit not booked:**


Text


```text
{{clinic_name}}: you don't have your next session booked yet. Book at {{booking_url}} or call {{clinic_phone}}. Reply STOP to opt out.
```


Characters: 134 as written.


### Lab and imaging


**Prep reminder:**


Text


```text
{{clinic_name}}: your visit is {{date}} at {{time}}. Check your portal for prep instructions: {{portal_url}} Reply STOP to opt out.
```


Characters: 131 as written.


**Results ready:**


Text


```text
{{clinic_name}}: you have new results. Sign in to view them: {{portal_url}} Questions? {{clinic_phone}}. Reply STOP to opt out.
```


Characters: 127 as written.


Prep instructions like fasting point to the test, so they live in the portal. Never name the test, the body part, or the result.


### Vaccines


**Appointment reminder:**


Text


```text
{{clinic_name}}: see you {{date}} at {{time}}. Please bring your vaccination record. Questions? {{clinic_phone}}. Reply STOP to opt out.
```


Characters: 136 as written.


**Next dose due:**


Text


```text
{{clinic_name}}: you're due for your next dose. Book at {{booking_url}} or call {{clinic_phone}}. Reply STOP to opt out.
```


Characters: 120 as written.


Leave out the vaccine name.


### Vision


**Exam reminder:**


Text


```text
{{clinic_name}}: see you {{date}} at {{time}}. If you wear glasses or contacts, bring them. Questions? {{clinic_phone}}. Reply STOP to opt out.
```


Characters: 143 as written.


**Yearly exam recall:**


Text


```text
{{clinic_name}}: it's time for your yearly exam. Book at {{booking_url}} or call {{clinic_phone}}. Reply STOP to opt out.
```


Characters: 121 as written.


## Opt-out, consent, and the TCPA healthcare exemption


Every text above ends with "Reply STOP to opt out." That covers the carrier side. The[CTIA Messaging Principles](https://api.ctia.org/wp-content/uploads/2023/05/230523-CTIA-Messaging-Principles-and-Best-Practices-FINAL.pdf) (section 5.1.3) expect you to:


- Tell recipients how to opt out
- Honor STOP, plus stop, end, unsubscribe, cancel, and quit
- Send one confirmation after an opt-out, then nothing further


The legal side is the TCPA. It has a specific exemption for healthcare messages from providers ([47 CFR 64.1200(a)(9)(iv)](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-47/part-64/section-64.1200) ), and appointment and exam confirmations and reminders are on its list of covered purposes. The conditions:


- The text isn't charged to the patient or counted against their plan limits
- It goes only to the number the patient gave you
- It names the provider and includes contact information
- It contains no telemarketing, advertising, billing, debt-collection, or financial content
- It complies with HIPAA
- It's 160 characters or less
- You send no more than one message a day and three a week per patient
- It tells recipients they can opt out by replying "STOP," which is the exclusive opt-out method, and you honor opt-outs immediately


Each template here names the provider and includes a phone number to fit those conditions. The first condition is the hard one to guarantee, since you don't control the patient's phone plan, so many practices collect consent anyway. Get legal review before you rely on the exemption.


The frequency cap adds up fast. Under the exemption, a booking confirmation, a 24-hour reminder, and a 2-hour reminder use all three of a week's texts, and a 2-hour reminder plus a day-of arrival text breaks the one-a-day limit. The cap covers calls and texts, so early reminders work well by email.


One more change is coming. Under[FCC 26-67](https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/10/26/2026-21821/enhancing-the-ability-of-consumers-to-control-the-robocalls) , effective November 25, 2026, you can designate an exclusive opt-out method if you disclose it clearly, an opt-out from one category of informational texts can apply to that category only, and revocations must be honored within a reasonable time of no more than ten business days. The[TCPA SMS rules for 2026](https://www.courier.com/blog/tcpa-sms-rules-2026) cover the details, and the[top 10 rules for SMS messaging](https://www.courier.com/blog/top-10-rules-for-sms-messaging) cover the basics.


## Timing and channel mix


Appointment type Sequence


Routine visit Email 72 hours before, SMS 24 hours before


Visit with prep or forms Email 7 days before, email 72 hours before, SMS 24 hours before


Telehealth Email 24 hours before, SMS 30 minutes before


Recall (checkup, cleaning, yearly exam) One email, then one SMS a week later if they haven't booked


A few rules hold across all of them:


- **SMS first for anything time-sensitive, with email as the fallback.** If a patient has no mobile number or has opted out of texts, send the email version.
- **Send in the patient's timezone, during their daytime.** A 6 AM reminder for a 9 AM visit helps no one.
- **Cancel queued reminders when the appointment moves.** A reminder for the old time is worse than no reminder at all. Send the reschedule confirmation instead.


## Send these automatically


The templates are the easy part. The work is sending each one at the right offset from the appointment, falling back to email when SMS can't reach someone, canceling queued reminders on a reschedule, and honoring opt-outs everywhere.


The[appointment reminder SMS recipe](https://www.courier.com/recipes/appointment-reminder-sms) does that in Courier with a journey: an email and SMS 24 hours out, one more text an hour before, and canceling or rescheduling the appointment cancels its reminders. To build it step by step, follow the[appointment reminder guide](https://www.courier.com/docs/guides/send-an-appointment-reminder) in the docs. Preview your texts on iPhone and Android with the[SMS preview generator](https://www.courier.com/tools/sms-preview-generator) , and check rendered lengths in the[SMS segment counter](https://www.courier.com/tools/sms-segment-counter) .


Courier maintains a HIPAA compliance program and signs BAAs with Enterprise customers. We recommend keeping PHI out of notification content either way, which is how every template above is written. See[HIPAA compliance and BAAs](https://www.courier.com/docs/security/hipaa) in the docs, and[HIPAA-compliant email](https://www.courier.com/blog/hipaa-compliant-email) for the email side. For more on how Courier supports care teams, see[Courier for healthcare](https://www.courier.com/solutions/healthcare) .


[Use these templates in Courier](https://app.courier.com/signup)


## Frequently asked questions


### What should an appointment reminder text say?


An appointment reminder text should say who it's from, the date and time, how to confirm or reschedule, and how to opt out. For example: "Maple Street Health: see you tomorrow at 9:30 AM. Reply C to confirm or R to reschedule. Questions? 555-201-4477. Reply STOP to opt out." Leave out the reason for the visit.


### How far in advance should you send appointment reminders?


Appointment reminders work best as a short sequence: an email two to three days before, then a text 24 hours before. Add a same-day text for telehealth links or arrival details, and send a week ahead for visits that need prep or paperwork.


### Can an appointment reminder text include the reason for the visit?


The reason for the visit should stay out of the text. A reminder lands on lock screens and shared phones, so keep it to the provider name, date, time, and location, and put visit details behind a login in your patient portal.


### Do I need consent to text appointment reminders?


Consent is the safe default. The TCPA has a healthcare exemption for appointment reminders, but it only applies when the text is free to the patient, 160 characters or less, and within one text a day and three a week. Collect consent when the patient shares their number, and get legal review before relying on the exemption.


### How long can an appointment reminder text be?


A single SMS segment holds 160 GSM-7 characters, and the TCPA healthcare exemption caps texts at 160 characters. One emoji or curly quote switches the encoding and drops the limit to 70, so stick to plain text and check the rendered length with real values filled in.


### Should I send appointment reminders by text or email?


Text and email work best together. Use email for early reminders with room for an address, prep notes, and a calendar link, and use SMS for the 24-hour and same-day nudges. If a patient opts out of texts or asks for email only, route everything to email.
